root_cause.text: In bcmgenet_put_txcb, the tx_cb pointer is computed from write_ptr before decrementing write_ptr, causing an off-by-one error where the next open descriptor is returned instead of the descriptor that was just completed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the calculation of tx_cb_ptr after the write_ptr rewinding logic, and the commit message states "The write_ptr points to the next open tx_cb. We want to return the tx_cb that gets rewinded, so we must rewind the pointer first then return the tx_cb that it points to."

candidates.rationale: Assigns the base pointer; the subsequent offset calculation uses the current write_ptr before decrement.
This computes the pointer using the pre-decrement write_ptr, causing off-by-one error (returns next descriptor instead of current).
Condition checks for wrap-around but is evaluated after the erroneous pointer calculation.
Decrement path (wrap) that should have been executed before pointer calculation; order is wrong.
Normal decrement path that should have been executed before pointer calculation; order is wrong.
Returns the incorrectly computed pointer, delivering wrong descriptor to caller.

Condition evaluated after pointer calculation; should have been evaluated before to correctly handle wrap-around.

Normal decrement path executed after pointer calculation, confirming the order bug.
